SuperAgent API 

# Build with the HivemindOS backend

 Add agents, memory, data, wallets, trading, media, and workflows to your own product. 

 
 Make your first call 
 Open the API reference 
 
 
 

The HivemindOS SuperAgent API lets your server use managed HivemindOS services. Your app sends a request, HivemindOS does the work, and your app gets the result. Paid work uses the same Agent Credit balance as the rest of HivemindOS.

It does **not** control a user's computer or open a desktop session.


| Resource | Address |
|---|---|
| API base | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1` |
| Private and confidential bases | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/private` and `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/confidential` ([what they include](privacy.html)) |
| Remote MCP | [`https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp`](https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp) |
| OpenAPI 3.1 contract | [`https://api.hivemindos.app/openapi.json`](https://api.hivemindos.app/openapi.json) |
| TypeScript package | `@hivemindos/sdk` |

sections.heading: 1. Get an API key
2. Make your first call
3. Read the result
sections.text:
Every JSON response has the same shape. Check `ok` first:

```json
{ "ok": true, "services": [] }
```

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": "This API key does not have access to that managed service." }
```

A failure may also include `code`, `operationId`, `metric`, and `retryAfterSeconds` so your app can decide what to do next. See [errors](runs-webhooks.html#error-envelope).

sections.heading: Or connect an agent with MCP
sections.text:
Add `https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp` as a remote Streamable HTTP server and send the key in a protected `Authorization` header. The agent gets four tools: list services, search allowed actions, read, and act. See [Connect an agent with MCP](mcp.html).

If your agent supports reusable skills, download [the SuperAgent API `SKILL.md`](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/SKILL.md) so it can keep managing keys, limits, funding, and tests.

sections.heading: How payment works
sections.text:
- Every key belongs to one HivemindOS account, and paid work uses that account's Agent Credits. A request cannot charge another account or set its own price.
- Wallet assets are separate: Agent Credits pay for managed work, while wallet assets pay transfer amounts, network fees, and trades.
- Managed database capacity follows the account's eligible plan.
- Read the current price with `GET /pricing` and the balance with `GET /credits/balance`. Show the returned final or maximum price before paid work starts.
- A key with `credits:write` can buy more Agent Credits with x402 through `POST /credits/x402/top-up`. HivemindOS fixes the recipient, network, asset, price, and credited account on the server. See the [reference](reference.html#x402-agent-credit-top-up).

sections.heading: Choose what to build
sections.text:
Give your app an agent 
 Run research, swarms, mini apps, media work, publishing, analytics, and scheduled workflows. 
 Browse managed services 
 
 
 Add long-term memory 
 Save facts and decisions, find them later, and answer from them. 
 Use managed memory 
 
 
 Store application data 
 Provision a managed database, then read and change records. 
 Use managed databases 
 
 
 Build safer money flows 
 Create managed wallets, ask for approvals, and run bounded transfers, signatures, trades, and any-token swaps. 
 Use wallets and trading 
 
 
 Run work in the background 
 Track long jobs, save their results, and get signed webhooks. 
 Use runs and webhooks 
 
 
 Control what a key can do 
 Allow only selected services and actions, then set request and spending limits. 
 Create a restricted key 
 
 

The catalog spans 33 stable service ids. The authenticated service catalog and capability registry are the source of truth: each capability has a stable operation id, access selector, method, path, approval mode, and run support.

sections.text:
# Set up the SuperAgent API with your agent

Your coding agent can set up the SuperAgent API in your project for you. You never copy a key: you open one link, sign in, add credits and approve, and the agent collects the key and saves it where your project keeps secrets.

sections.heading: Set it up
sections.text:
1. On [hivemindos.app/superagent-api](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/#setup), press **Copy** in "Set it up with your agent".
2. Paste it into the agent working in your project (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, or any agent that can run commands) and send it.
3. The agent gives you a link and a short code. Open the link and check the code matches.
4. **Sign in or make an account** with your email. One code does both, and the account works on any device. A passkey works too, or you can continue without an email and add one later.
5. **Add credits** by card or crypto, from $5, or choose Later.
6. **Approve.** The page says the account is ready, then shows "your agent has your key" once the agent collects it.

The agent saves the key as `HIVEMINDOS_API_KEY` in your project's `.env.local` or `.env`, makes sure git ignores that file, checks the key works, and tells you your credit balance.

A setup link lasts 60 minutes and can be approved once. The key it makes can use every service but can never move funds: it can't sign, send or trade from a wallet, approve actions, or manage other keys. Those stay with you.

sections.heading: If your agent can't run commands
sections.text:
Chat apps such as ChatGPT and Claude on the web can't collect the key themselves. Either:

- on the setup link, after approving, open **Using a chat that can't save files?** and press **Show my key** to see the key and the exact `.env` line; or
- make a key yourself in the [console](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/console/#keys).

sections.heading: What the agent does
sections.text:
The setup message points the agent at [hivemindos.app/superagent-api/llms.txt](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/llms.txt). With Node.js 18 or newer, the agent runs a small dependency-free script, [setup.mjs](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/setup.mjs), that does every step below and never prints the key. If the command times out, running it again continues the same setup.

Without Node, the agent calls the API directly:

1. `POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/setup-sessions` with a label and its name. No key is needed. The response has your link (`setupUrl`), the code (`confirmCode`), and a `claimToken` the agent keeps secret. Use `/v1/private/setup-sessions` to pin the key to the [private tier](privacy.html).
2. It shows you the link and the code.
3. It calls `POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/setup-sessions/claim` with `Authorization: Bearer ` every 5 seconds. The answer is `202` until you approve, then `200` with the key. If that reply is lost, the same claim token returns the same key for 10 minutes.
4. It saves the key and checks it with `GET /v1/services` and `GET /v1/credits/balance`.

sections.heading: Let the agent pay for the account
sections.text: An agent with an x402 wallet on Base can pay for the account itself, after you approve the exact amount. It calls `POST /v1/setup-sessions/fund` with its claim token and an `Idempotency-Key`, answers the payment challenge, and gets the key straight away. You then open the same link to take over the account and add your email to keep it.

sections.heading: Let the integration buy more credits
sections.text:
Give the key the `credits:write` scope and the `credits.x402.topUp` operation. The agent can then add an x402-aware client that pays Base payment challenges and credits the same HivemindOS account.

1. The first request gets an HTTP 402 payment challenge.
2. The agent asks you to confirm the exact dollar amount. Top-ups may be $5 to $500.
3. The wallet client signs and retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
4. Success returns a receipt and the updated Agent Credit balance.

HivemindOS fixes and verifies the official revenue wallet, payment network, asset, amount, and credited account, so the integration cannot redirect the payment. See the [reference](reference.html#x402-agent-credit-top-up) for exact headers and fields.

sections.heading: Keep it as a reusable skill
sections.text:
If your agent supports skills, download [hivemindos.app/superagent-api/SKILL.md](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/SKILL.md) and install it the way that agent installs skills. The skill lets the agent keep managing access, endpoint limits, MCP, capabilities, Agent Credits, tests, and audits for the project.

If the agent supports remote MCP servers, it can also connect directly to `https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp` with the same key. See [Connect an agent with MCP](mcp.html).

sections.heading: Manage keys and billing
sections.text: The [console](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/console/) shows your balance, keys, usage, request history, limits, projects and privacy tiers. Make or revoke keys there, and add credits to the one balance every service draws on.

sections.heading: Checklist for a finished setup
sections.text:
- The app loads its key from private runtime settings, on the server only.
- The key reaches only the services and actions you chose.
- Endpoint request and concurrency limits are set.
- Balance, service, and capability checks pass through the app's real client.
- A deliberately disallowed capability is denied, when practical to test.
- Mutations use idempotency keys.
- No secret appears in the project diff, logs, tests, or docs.

# AI web search

The `answer-engine` service searches the web, reads the pages that matter, and writes an answer with numbered citations. You send a question and get back the answer plus the sources it was built from.

The request and response shapes match the open-source [Vane](https://github.com/ItzCrazyKns/Vane) search API, so a Vane client works here with only the address and authorization header changed.

sections.heading: Ask a question
Choose how hard it looks
sections.text:
| `optimizationMode` | What it does | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `speed` | One search pass, answers from search results | Quick lookups |
| `balanced` | A few search passes, reads the best pages | The everyday default |
| `quality` | Many search passes, reads more pages, writes a report | Research worth the extra time and credits |

sections.heading: Choose where to look
sections.text:
`sources` picks which parts of the web are searched. Ask for more than one when the question needs both.

| Lane | Covers |
|---|---|
| `web` | The open web |
| `discussions` | Forums and community answers |
| `academic` | Papers, preprints, and journals |
| `documents` | Text you sent with the request |

A lane is used only when the question calls for it, so asking for all of them costs nothing extra on a question that needs none.

To limit sites, pass `includeDomains` (search only these) or `excludeDomains` (never these). Plain site addresses work; `https://` and trailing slashes are tidied away.

```ts
const result = await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "answer-engine",
 "searches.create",
 { query: "transformer scaling laws", includeDomains: ["arxiv.org", "nature.com"] },
 { idempotencyKey: "scaling-laws-001" },
);
```

sections.heading: Answer from your own documents
Extras
sections.text:
- **Images and videos:** set `includeMedia: true` and they come back alongside the answer, but only when they help ("what does a heat pump look like" gets images, "what does a heat pump cost" does not). Images carry their licence and source page. You can also call `images.search` or `videos.search` on their own with a `query`.
- **Instant answers:** arithmetic, currency conversion, weather, and crypto prices come back in a `widgets` array with the answer already worked out, at no extra model cost. Share prices are not offered, because there is no keyless quote source HivemindOS trusts.
- **Follow-up questions:** set `includeSuggestions: true` to get a few follow-ups aimed at what the answer left open.

sections.heading: Stream the answer
sections.text:
Set `stream: true` to receive the answer as it is written, as newline-delimited JSON (one object per line):

| Frame | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `init` | The stream is open |
| `session` | The search's id, for reconnecting |
| `step` | Progress: what is being searched or read now |
| `widget` | An instant answer |
| `media` | Images or videos, when asked for |
| `sources` | The full source list, sent before the answer text |
| `response` | A piece of the answer |
| `suggestions` | Follow-up questions, when asked for |
| `error` | Something went wrong; the stream still closes cleanly |
| `done` | The answer is complete |

Show `step` frames to display progress, or ignore them and wait for `response`.

If the connection drops, reconnect with the id from the `session` frame (also in the `x-hivemindos-answer-session` header):

```ts
await hive.services.invokeOperation("answer-engine", "searches.reconnect", {}, {
 pathParameters: { searchId },
 idempotencyKey: `reconnect-${searchId}`,
});
```

Everything produced so far replays, then live frames continue. The search keeps running while you are disconnected, so no paid model time is lost. You can reconnect for fifteen minutes after the answer finishes.

sections.heading: Models and cost
sections.text:
List answer models with `models.list`. Pass a `chatModel` to pick one, or leave it out for the recommended default. Answers are billed to the same Agent Credit balance as the rest of the API, and this service adds no charge on top of the model it uses.

The HivemindOS desktop app has the same search under **Search**, where it can use a model on your own computer so nothing leaves it.

sections.heading: What it will not do
sections.text:
- Answer from memory when the sources do not cover the question. It says what is missing instead.
- Cite a page it did not retrieve.
- Repeat one story five times because five outlets carried it: near-identical results fold into one citation.
- Follow instructions found on a web page. Page text is treated as untrusted content.

# Authentication and API keys

An API key lets your backend call HivemindOS for one account. Keep it on your server, give it only the access its job needs, and replace it if it is ever exposed.

The safe default: one key per app or worker, allowed only the services and actions it needs, with limits, and with approval power kept on a different key.

sections.heading: Authenticate requests
sections.text:
Send the key as a bearer token:

```bash
curl https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/services \
 --header "Authorization: Bearer $HIVEMINDOS_API_KEY"
```

Never put the key in a URL or request body. A browser or mobile client should call your backend, which then calls HivemindOS.

The remote MCP at `https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp` uses the same key. See [MCP](mcp.html).

sections.heading: Create the first key
sections.text:
The quickest way is the [console](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/console/#keys) or [agent setup](agent-setup.html). To do it through the API, use an existing HivemindOS credit token once. This is the only request that accepts `X-HivemindOS-Credit-Token` instead of a bearer key.

```bash
curl https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/api-keys \
 --request POST \
 --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
 --header "Idempotency-Key: backend-root-key-v1" \
 --header "X-HivemindOS-Credit-Token: $HIVEMINDOS_CREDIT_TOKEN" \
 --data '{
 "label": "Backend root",
 "scopes": [
 "services:read",
 "services:invoke",
 "credits:read",
 "api_keys:manage"
 ],
 "allowedServices": ["hive-research", "managed-workflows"],
 "allowedOperations": [
 "actions.list",
 "services.invoke.hive-research.analyses.create",
 "runs.create.hive-research.analyses.create"
 ],
 "expiresAt": "2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
 }'
```

The response includes `secret`, an `hmos_live_...` value returned only this once. Save it in your secret manager right away. Later listings show only a prefix and metadata.

sections.heading: Key expiry
sections.text:
Keys expire by default. Leave out `expiresAt` and a key lasts 30 days:

| How the key was made | Without `expiresAt` | With `expiresAt` |
|---|---|---|
| From a credit token | 30 days, renewed by use: each authenticated request moves the expiry to 30 days from then. Repeating the same create request (same idempotency key and input) also renews it, even after it expired. | Fixed at that time. |
| From another key | 30 days, fixed, and never later than its parent. | Fixed at that time, and never later than its parent. |

- A chosen `expiresAt` is never moved, and it can be at most 365 days away.
- A key that can move funds or approve (`wallets:sign`, `wallets:transact`, `approvals:write`, or `trading:execute`) can be given at most 90 days.
- Each key reports `expiresAt`. An expired key answers `401`; so do all its descendants, since a child never outlives its parent. Rotate before the date (see [below](#rotate-or-revoke-a-key)), or keep using a renewing key.

sections.heading: What decides a key's access
sections.text:
A request must pass all four checks:

1. **Scopes**: which kinds of actions the key may perform. See the [scope list](reference.html#scopes).
2. **Service access**: which managed services it may reach.
3. **Operation access**: which exact capabilities and endpoints it may call.
4. **Limits**: how often or how much it may use each operation. See [per-endpoint limits](limits.html).

sections.heading: Choose service access
sections.text:
Use one of these fields when creating a key, not both:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `allowedServices` | The key can reach only the listed service ids. The safest default for production. |
| `excludedServices` | Every service available at creation except these. Saved as an explicit allowlist, so services added later stay excluded. |
| Neither field | The key inherits its parent's service boundary. A root key without a boundary may use any service its scopes permit, including ones added later. |

An empty `allowedServices` array blocks every managed service but still permits non-service operations covered by the key's scopes.

Database, wallet, and trading routes follow the same boundary through `hivemind-database`, `managed-wallets`, and `managed-trading`.

sections.heading: Choose operation access
sections.text:
Use `allowedOperations` to allow only exact capabilities and endpoints, or `excludedOperations` to remove some from the parent's boundary. Do not send both.

```json
{
 "allowedOperations": [
 "capabilities.list",
 "services.invoke.hive-research.analyses.create",
 "runs.create.hive-research.analyses.create",
 "runs.read"
 ]
}
```

- Operation access is fixed when the key is created. New capabilities added later do not become reachable on their own.
- An aggregate selector such as `services.invoke.hive-research` covers all of that service's registered operations. An exact selector such as `services.invoke.hive-research.analyses.create` covers one.
- Include the supporting operations a workflow needs. A worker that permanently deletes managed memory needs `services.invoke.cloud-superbrain.memory.delete` together with `approvals.create` and `approvals.decide`. A key that revokes itself also needs `apiKeys.revoke`. Supporting operations do not widen the key's service boundary.

A project-bound key is permanently restricted to one project, and so are all its children. See [projects and isolation](projects-security.html).

sections.heading: Use idempotency keys
sections.text:
Every mutation and spending action requires `Idempotency-Key`. Use a stable id for one logical action, such as your order or job id:

```http
Idempotency-Key: order_01J6M1Q64NQH8S1QKC9D7G3V3T
```

- 8–200 characters: letters, digits, colons, periods, underscores, and hyphens.
- The same key with the same input returns the stored result. The same key with different input returns HTTP 409.
- Keys are isolated per API key, so two sibling keys can use the same external job id safely.

sections.heading: Give each responsibility its own key
sections.text:
- A catalog key with only read scopes.
- One worker key per service or workload.
- A funding key with `credits:read` and `credits:write`, restricted to `credits.balance.read` and `credits.x402.topUp`.
- A wallet execution key without approval authority.
- A reviewer key with `approvals:write` but no wallet or trading execution scope.
- A key-management key kept away from ordinary workers.

A compromised component then cannot reach unrelated services or approve the action it proposed.

A funding key decides who may ask your x402 payer to buy Agent Credits. It cannot choose the revenue wallet or credit another account. Keep the payer's signer in a separate secret store and have your user approve each payment before signing.

sections.heading: Delegate narrower child keys
Rotate or revoke a key
sections.text:
1. Create a new child key with the same or narrower policy.
2. Add it to your secret manager.
3. Move traffic to the new key and confirm requests succeed.
4. Revoke the old key with `DELETE /api-keys/{id}` and a unique idempotency key.

Revocation is immediate. It also stops webhooks created under that key from receiving new events.

# Memory benchmarks

 What SuperAgent API memory is measured to do, on public benchmarks, with every answer published. 

Two surfaces share one memory design: **hosted memory** (the Cloud Superbrain behind this API's `memory.*` operations) and the **Hive Superbrain** that runs on your own computer (`hive-brain answer`). They recall the same way; the hosted Memory Answer works within one 24,000-character budget, while the computer version can hand over up to 60,000. Each result below says which one it measures.

These are measured snapshots, not an availability or latency promise.

sections.heading: Hosted memory (this API)
sections.text:
| Measure | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Search: the chats that hold the answer are in `memory.recall`'s top 5 (recall@5), LongMemEval_S, `rerank: true` | **97.68%** (hit@5 99.4%) |
| The same without `rerank: true` (meaning search on) | **93.71%** |
| Evidence reaches the reading model, LongMemEval_S, `memory.answer` with meaning search and Turbo | **96.17%** |
| Evidence reaches the reading model, LongMemEval_S (each answer among ~50 past chats) | **90.6%** |
| Evidence reaches the reading model, LongMemEval Oracle (only the chats that hold the answer) | **98.5%** |
| Answers correct, 150 LongMemEval_S questions | **81.9%** |

Search (measured 2026-09-28): all 500 questions through the real memory routes with the production embedding model, scored with sibyl.ist's open LongMemEval_S metric code; before these changes recall@5 was 90.69% and the Turbo answer's evidence 91.91%. [Method and per-type results](https://hivemindos.app/docs/for-users/features/shared-brain-benchmarks.html#hosted-memory-search-accuracy). Earlier evidence rows: all 500 questions (470 answerable), `memory.answer` in keyword order, no model calls. Answers: the shipped reader, graded by LongMemEval's own judge prompts with `gpt-4o-mini`, measured on 2026-09-23 and not yet re-run on the current evidence layout.

sections.heading: Choosing a reader
sections.text:
In a second run, other models read the same 150 questions with the same evidence; the default reader scored 80.7% in that run. Share answered correctly, and the reader's median time (the model's own time, not the whole request):

| Reader | Correct | Median time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` | 82.1% | 4.0 s |
| `@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8` (default) | 80.7% | 4.0 s |
| `@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash` | 80.3% | 18.7 s |
| `@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` | 78.7% | 23.0 s |
| `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b`, low effort | 78.0% | 2.2 s |
| `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-20b`, low effort | 69.3% | 1.3 s |
| `@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` | 68.7% | 2.0 s |
| `@cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct` | 54.0% | 1.6 s |

DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM 4.7 Flash returned no answer for 5 and 3 questions; their shares count the questions they answered (119 of 145 and 118 of 147), and over all 150 they are 79.3% and 78.7%. Scores within a few points of each other are within this sample's noise. To pick a reader, see [Choose who reads the answer](memory.html#choose-who-reads-the-answer).

sections.heading: Behavior and latency
sections.text:
The August 27, 2026 authenticated API benchmark used three fresh isolated hosted accounts. Every account passed all eight lexical behavior cases, all six semantic Top-1 cases, and all three grounded-answer cases, including aliases, current and historical evolution, usage ranking, operational isolation, paraphrases, and unsupported-question abstention. The equivalent local typed-memory cases also passed in every fresh run.

Hosted recall is slower than the local vault path. Measured on September 30, 2026 as server time (`Server-Timing`), on a brain of 20 short memories: keyword search (`memory.search`) takes about 24 ms; semantic recall (`memory.recall`) 333 ms median (416 ms p90), most of it the meaning index (about 200 ms) and embedding the question (about 90 ms); a Memory Answer with the default reader 665 ms median, of which the answer model is about 360 ms. `rerank: true` adds about 1 s. Answers that read long conversation histories take longer, almost all of it the answering model. Network time comes on top: from the Philippines, a semantic recall took about 480 ms end to end. The local lexical/API behavior trials had a median p50 of 7.85 milliseconds.

The August 27 trials above were timed before the second read (`rerank: true` and Turbo) and the current recall, so their times no longer describe the service; they are kept with the quality results on the [benchmarks page](https://hivemindos.app/docs/for-users/features/shared-brain-benchmarks.html#hosted-superagent-api-memory).

These results support quality parity on the published cases, not universal parity with every private vault.

sections.heading: Hive Superbrain (same design, on your computer)
sections.text:
Claude Opus 4.6 reads what memory returns; LongMemEval's official judge prompts with `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` grade every answer.

| Benchmark | Hive Superbrain | Compared with |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| LongMemEval Oracle, 470 questions | **96.6%** | Sibyl-Memory's published Opus 4.6 answers, graded the same way: 95.3% (p = 0.33) |
| LongMemEval_S, 470 questions | **94.3%** | Sibyl-Memory's published architecture, run with its public runner: 92.1% (p = 0.16), reading about a ninth of the tokens |
| LoCoMo, 500 questions | **94.4%** | A pre-registered held-out test: none of the memory design was tuned on LoCoMo |

HivemindOS scored higher than Sibyl-Memory on both comparisons; neither difference is established beyond chance.

sections.heading: Receipts
sections.text: Every context memory returned, every answer and every verdict is published in [hivemindos-memory-benchmarks](https://github.com/LiamVisionary/hivemindos-memory-benchmarks), with scripts that recompute each number from the files. # Capabilities, agents, workflows, and mini apps

A **service** is a managed product area, such as research or memory. A **capability** is one action inside it, such as creating an analysis or recalling a memory.

1. List the capabilities your key can use.
2. Pick a stable operation id.
3. Call it now, or create a [durable run](runs-webhooks.html#durable-runs) for longer work.

sections.heading: List capabilities
sections.text:
```ts
const response = await hive.services.capabilities();
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(response.error);

for (const capability of response.capabilities) {
 console.log(
 capability.serviceId,
 capability.id,
 capability.operationId,
 capability.approval,
 );
}
```

Filter to one service with `hive.services.capabilities("managed-agents")` or `GET /capabilities/{serviceId}`. Results only include what the key's service and operation boundary allows. The registry also marks work that is not currently available.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Stable id within the service, such as `agents.create`. |
| `operationId` | Exact selector for direct invocation or a dedicated SuperAgent API route. |
| `runOperationId` | Exact background-run selector, or `null` for a dedicated route. |
| `method` and `path` | Reviewed managed-service contract and path parameters. |
| `mode` | `read`, `write`, or `execute`. |
| `idempotent` | Whether the operation requires a protected idempotent mutation. |
| `approval` | `never`, `policy`, or `always`. |
| `asynchronous` | Whether the service normally keeps working after accepting the request. |

sections.heading: Call a capability
Attach files
sections.text:
Capabilities with `requestFormat: "multipart"` take [managed files](files-connections.html) by id. Upload once, then attach the file to calls or runs:

```ts
await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "distill",
 "runs.create",
 { skillName: "Customer interview analyst" },
 {
 fileIds: [uploaded.file.id],
 idempotencyKey: "distill-interviews-v1",
 },
);
```

The key needs `files:read`. One call can attach up to 40 files with a combined 25 MB limit.

Capabilities with `requestFormat: "binary"` take exactly one managed file. `hive-compute.artifacts.upload` uses this for encrypted workload input: the API takes the ciphertext digest from the managed file record and checks the encryption metadata before forwarding the bytes. It never accepts a caller-supplied digest.

What the registry covers
sections.text:
- Persistent cloud agents, agent chat, app building, integrations, and governed computer actions through `managed-agents`.
- Scheduled, manual, and event-driven routines through `managed-workflows`.
- Research, multi-agent swarms, audience discovery, transcripts, skill distillation, market intelligence, and lead data.
- Managed model inference, media generation, photo analysis, GPU rentals, and Hive Compute jobs.
- Typed, evolving cloud memory through `cloud-superbrain`, and portable application data through `hivemind-database`.
- App hosting, bookings, social publishing, email, analytics, X operations, calendar access, and remote tool servers.
- Token research, wallet risk, bridge quotes, copy-trading monitors, managed wallets, and managed spot trading.

Every capability, including `hive-compute`, `testnet-faucet`, and managed mini-app backends, bills the same account's Agent Credits. Failed work releases its reservation, and completed work reports its exact charge in the result, response header, usage records, and audit records. Mini-app backends run without a desktop session and never copy their protected credentials into your product.

# Hive Compute and testnet assets

Use Hive Compute (`hive-compute`) when an agent needs hosted GPU work. Use the testnet faucet (`testnet-faucet`) when a developer needs test assets with no monetary value. Both use the account's Agent Credits and need no desktop session.

| If you need | Start with |
|---|---|
| A model response or generated image | [Managed inference](#run-managed-inference) |
| The best live GPU offer | [Marketplace search](#search-the-compute-marketplace) |
| Private GPU work with verified hardware | [Confidential workload](#run-a-confidential-asynchronous-workload) |
| A test wallet funded for development | [Testnet assets](#request-testnet-assets) |

Main compute operations: `marketplace.search`, `models.list`, `chat.create`, `images.create`, `jobs.create`, `artifacts.upload`, and `artifacts.get`. `marketplace.listings` and `marketplace.status` show live offers and capacity. Faucet operations: `assets.list`, `claims.create`, and `claims.get`. Read the full live set with `GET /capabilities/{serviceId}`.

Every successful call reports its exact charge in `chargedCredits`. Failed work releases its reservation.

Run managed inference

sections.text:
The Hive Compute MCP server is a smaller alternative to the [full SuperAgent MCP](mcp.html) for agents that only need the GPU marketplace. It calls the same operations, with the same key permissions, limits, and credit balance.

```text
URL: https://compute-mcp.hivemindos.app/mcp
Authentication: Authorization: Bearer hmos_live_...
Transport: Streamable HTTP
```

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `hive_compute_search` | Resolve privacy, search live offers, compare trust, and quote credits. |
| `hive_compute_chat` | Run non-streaming chat inference against the selected offer. |
| `hive_compute_image` | Generate images against the selected offer. |
| `hive_compute_job_create` | Create a Confidential Verified asynchronous workload draft. |
| `hive_compute_job_status` | Read asynchronous job status. |
| `hive_compute_job_cancel` | Cancel a job and release unused reservation. |

Give the agent the smallest key it needs: a search-only agent can be limited to `services.invoke.hive-compute.marketplace.search`, and a chat agent can add `services.invoke.hive-compute.chat.create` with its own request, daily, credit, and concurrency ceilings. Only use clients that can store a bearer key securely; clients that require OAuth for remote MCP are not supported yet.

sections.heading: Create a tightly limited key
sections.text:
```ts
const issued = await createHivemindOSApiKey({
 creditToken: process.env.HIVEMINDOS_CREDIT_TOKEN!,
 label: "Compute and testnet backend",
 scopes: ["services:read", "services:invoke", "files:read", "files:write"],
 allowedServices: ["hive-compute", "testnet-faucet"],
 allowedOperations: [
 "capabilities.list",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.marketplace.search",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.marketplace.listings",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.marketplace.status",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.models.list",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.chat.create",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.images.create",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.jobs.create",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.jobs.get",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.jobs.submit",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.artifacts.upload",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.artifacts.get",
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.artifacts.acknowledge",
 "services.invoke.testnet-faucet.assets.list",
 "services.invoke.testnet-faucet.claims.create",
 "services.invoke.testnet-faucet.claims.get",
 ],
 limits: {
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.marketplace.search": {
 requestsPerMinute: 60,
 maxConcurrent: 8,
 },
 "services.invoke.hive-compute.chat.create": {
 requestsPerMinute: 20,
 maxConcurrent: 4,
 },
 "services.invoke.testnet-faucet.claims.create": {
 requestsPerDay: 10,
 maxConcurrent: 1,
 },
 },
 idempotencyKey: "compute-testnet-key-v1",
});
```

Drop the file scopes and artifact operations when a key only needs chat, images, or faucet claims.

# Managed databases

Managed databases give your app a private place for structured records, such as customers, tasks, inventory, or saved results. The data belongs to the authenticated account and project.

Most apps need three steps: provision the workspace once, create a table, then read and change records.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.text:
Use a key with:

- `hivemind-database` in its service boundary;
- `databases:read` for status, structure, records, and transfer status; and
- `databases:write` for provisioning, changes, uploads, downloads, and cancellation.

Use the SDK's database methods; they keep access, confirmation, file-size, and workspace rules consistent.

sections.heading: Check the account
Provision the workspace
Create tables and records
Read structure and records
sections.text:
Queries use `POST /databases/query` with `databases:read`. They are read-only and need no idempotency key.

```ts
const records = await hive.databases.query({
 action: "list-records",
 tableId: 42,
 page: 1,
 pageSize: 50,
 orderBy: "created_at desc",
});

if (!records.ok) throw new Error(records.error);
```

| Action | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `list-workspaces` | None |
| `list-databases` | `workspaceId` |
| `list-tables` | `databaseId` |
| `list-fields` | `tableId` |
| `list-records` | `tableId`; optional `page`, `pageSize`, `search`, `orderBy` |
| `get-record` | `tableId`, `recordId` |

# Files, connections, and integrations

Upload a **file** when a managed service needs source material. Create a **connection** when a service needs another account or tool, without exposing that credential to your app's workers.

File lists show metadata, never file bytes. Connection lists show labels and field names, never secret values.

sections.heading: Upload a file
sections.text:
```ts
const uploaded = await hive.files.upload(
 {
 name: "customer-brief.pdf",
 contentType: "application/pdf",
 bytes: new Uint8Array(await readFile("customer-brief.pdf")),
 purpose: "research-source",
 },
 { idempotencyKey: "customer-brief-pdf-v1" },
);
```

Files must be between 1 byte and 25 MB. The API calculates a SHA-256 checksum; pass a known one in `sha256` and the upload fails if it does not match.

List metadata with `files.list()`, download bytes with `files.download(id)`, and delete with `files.remove(id)`. A deleted file cannot be recreated by replaying its old idempotency key.

Over raw HTTP, send the bytes as the request body with these headers:

| Header | Use |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | File media type. |
| `Content-Length` | File size in bytes. |
| `X-File-Name` | Customer-visible file name. |
| `X-Content-Sha256` | Optional expected checksum. |
| `X-HivemindOS-File-Purpose` | Optional project-defined purpose. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | Stable identifier for one logical upload. |

sections.heading: Store a connection
Use a connection
sections.text:
Pass the connection id when a capability needs it:

```ts
await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "hive-research",
 "tier.get",
 undefined,
 {
 connectionId: created.connection.id,
 idempotencyKey: "connected-tier-check-001",
 },
);
```

HivemindOS supplies the credential to the operation and updates `lastVerifiedAt` after a successful response. The value is never returned.

- The caller needs `connections:read`, and the connection must be active.
- A connection bound to one service cannot be used with another.
- For capabilities marked `approval: "always"`, send the same `connectionId` in both the [approval request](capabilities-agents.html#create-a-protected-action-approval) and the call.

sections.heading: Calendar and remote tool integrations
sections.text:
The `integration-broker` service connects Google Calendar and remote MCP servers without returning their OAuth or bearer credentials. Useful capability ids:

- `connections.list`
- `google.oauth.start`
- `google.calendar.events.create`
- `mcp.connections.create`
- `mcp.invoke`
- `connections.revoke`

`google.oauth.start` returns an authorization URL for the account owner; the provider completes the connection directly with HivemindOS. Calendar writes, new remote-tool connections, and revocations need an input-bound approval. Remote tool calls also follow the broker's method and confirmation policy.

sections.heading: Keep credentials safe
sections.text:
- Create and rotate credentials from a narrow, project-bound key.
- Give workers `connections:read` only when they need connection metadata, and keep `connections:write` away from workloads that use the connected service.
- Pass a `connectionId` instead of retrieving and forwarding a credential yourself.
- When you retire an integration, delete the connection and revoke the provider-side grant.

# Per-endpoint limits

Limits stop one key or worker from using more than you intended. For each endpoint you can cap requests per minute, hour, or day, how many run at once, and, for selected money operations, Agent Credits spent per day.

Limits are fixed when the key is created. To change them, create a replacement key.

sections.heading: Set limits on a key
Limit fields
sections.text:
| Field | Meaning | Accepted maximum |
|---|---|---:|
| `requestsPerMinute` | Requests during a fixed minute window. | 60,000 |
| `requestsPerHour` | Requests during a fixed hour window. | 1,000,000 |
| `requestsPerDay` | Requests during a fixed UTC day. | 10,000,000 |
| `maxConcurrent` | Requests for the selector that may be in progress at once. | 1,000 |
| `creditsPerDay` | Agent Credits the selector may spend during a fixed UTC day. | 1,000,000,000 |
| `creditsPerCall` | The most one call may cost, in Agent Credits. See [the most one call may cost](#most-one-call-may-cost). | 1,000,000,000 |

- Request and concurrency values must be positive integers. `creditsPerDay` must be positive with at most three decimal places. `creditsPerCall` may be 0 (free calls only) or more, with at most three decimal places.
- A key may define at most 128 selectors.
- The maximums are validation ceilings, not default quotas. An omitted field adds no limit, but account balance, plan allowance, service availability, wallet policy, and ancestor-key limits still apply.
- Concurrent capacity stays in use until the response finishes, including a streamed one. Always consume or cancel response bodies.

sections.heading: Limit selectors
sections.text:
The `limits` object is keyed by operation id:

| Selector | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `*` | Every authenticated SuperAgent API operation. |
| A static operation such as `databases.actions` | Only that endpoint operation. |
| `services.invoke` | Every direct managed-service invocation. |
| `services.invoke. ` | Direct invocation of one managed service. |
| `services.invoke. . ` | One exact registered capability invoked directly. |
| `runs.create` | Every durable run creation. |
| `runs.create. ` | Run creation for one managed service. |
| `runs.create. . ` | One exact registered capability created as a run. |

Every matching selector applies, and the request is rejected as soon as any one is used up. For `hive-research` operation `analyses.create`, the API checks `*`, `services.invoke`, `services.invoke.hive-research`, and `services.invoke.hive-research.analyses.create`. Likewise, `services.invoke.cloud-superbrain.memory.answer` limits memory answers alone, while `services.invoke.cloud-superbrain` caps every Cloud Superbrain operation.

The SDK exports every accepted operation id as `HIVEMINDOS_PLATFORM_OPERATION_IDS`; they are also in the [endpoint reference](reference.html#limit-operation-ids).

sections.heading: Daily credit limits
sections.text:
`creditsPerDay` can be set on `*` or on any operation. A new key gets 2,000 a day on `*` unless it names its own `*` limits.

- The operations the API bills itself hold their whole quoted charge against the limit before they start, and only the final charge counts: `wallets.create`, `wallets.transactions.create`, `wallets.signatures.create`, `trading.orders.create` and `swaps.execute`.
- Every other call is checked before it runs against what the key has already spent today, and its charge is counted after it answers. The last call before the limit can therefore finish past it by at most its own charge.

A key's credit limit does not add credits and does not replace wallet policy. A request must pass the key limit, have enough account credits, and satisfy the wallet's own rules.

`credits.x402.topUp` accepts request and concurrency limits but not `creditsPerDay`, because it buys credits rather than spending them. The unsigned HTTP 402 challenge does not use up a request slot; the first signed payment attempt does, and an idempotent replay of a completed top-up does not.

sections.heading: The most one call may cost
sections.text:
`creditsPerCall` holds every call a key makes to a ceiling, and `maxCredits` in an invoke body (or the `X-HivemindOS-Max-Credits` header) does the same for one call. The lower of the two decides. A call runs only when its price is known before it starts and fits:

- An operation with a published maximum (most operations sold per call, and those whose service lists one) runs if that maximum fits. Otherwise it is refused with HTTP 409, `code: price_above_maximum`, and its `priceCredits`.
- A free operation always runs, even under 0.
- An operation priced only after it runs (a model reply, a metered lookup) is refused with HTTP 409 and `code: price_not_known_up_front`. One priced by a free quote says which quote operation to ask first.

Nothing is charged for a refused call, and it never reaches the service. `GET /inspect/{serviceId}/{operationId}` shows any operation's price before you call it, keyless and free.

sections.heading: Pause a key
sections.text: `PATCH /api-keys/{id}` with `{"paused": true}` stops a key, and every key made from it, without revoking it: each call is refused with HTTP 403 and `code: api_key_paused`, which names the paused key. `{"paused": false}` resumes it, with its limits, scopes and expiry as they were. A key may pause itself or a key made from it; only a key above it, or the account in the console on hivemindos.app, may resume it. The same route changes a key's `limits` in place, merged into what it has, and never past a key above it.

sections.heading: Child keys and ancestor limits
sections.text:
Every key above a child still applies its limits. If a root key allows 1,000 requests per hour and its child allows 100, the child gets 100. A child cannot set a covering limit higher than an ancestor's, and leaving a limit out does not bypass the parent. Revoking or expiring any ancestor invalidates the child.

Use this to set organization-wide ceilings on the root key and smaller budgets on each worker.

sections.heading: Handle HTTP 429
sections.text:
When a key hits a request, concurrency, or daily-credit limit, the API returns HTTP 429:

```json
{
 "ok": false,
 "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
 "error": "This API key has reached its request limit for this operation.",
 "operationId": "services.invoke.hive-research",
 "metric": "requestsPerMinute",
 "retryAfterSeconds": 18
}
```

With these headers:

```http
Retry-After: 18
X-HivemindOS-Limit-Operation: services.invoke.hive-research
```

Pause that workload for at least `retryAfterSeconds`. Queueing work in your backend is usually better than having every caller retry. Another operation may still have capacity, but do not route around a deliberate key-wide or ancestor limit.

```ts
const result = await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "hive-research",
 "analyses.create",
 { question: "..." },
 { idempotencyKey: jobId },
);

if (!result.ok && result.code === "rate_limit_exceeded") {
 await queueForLater(jobId, result.retryAfterSeconds ?? 60);
}
```

# Connect an agent with MCP

MCP is the simplest way to let an agent use HivemindOS managed services. The agent searches the actions its key allows, reads data, and runs approved work, without you writing a wrapper for each endpoint.

```text
MCP address: https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp
Transport: Streamable HTTP
Authentication: Authorization: Bearer hmos_live_...
```

sections.heading: Connect it
Give it a narrow key
What the agent gets
sections.text:
Four stable tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `hive_services_list` | List services the key may use and optionally check live availability. |
| `hive_actions_search` | Find exact allowed actions and their input, approval, and execution details. |
| `hive_read` | Run an action marked read-only. It refuses writes and execution. |
| `hive_write` | Run a write or execution action with a stable idempotency key. It refuses reads. |

Search results are filtered by the key, so a restricted key cannot discover or call an excluded service or operation.

sections.heading: One tool per operation
sections.text:
Some apps pick from a fixed tool list instead of searching, such as Meta Muse connectors and chat apps with a tool picker. Connect those to:

```text
https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp?tools=operations
```

This adds one tool per operation, named ` __ `, such as `svg-studio__svgs_generate` or `token-autopsy__reports_create`. Each tool describes its input with an example, its price, and how to collect a background result. Add `&services=svg-studio,leadgen-data` to list only the services your app uses.

These tools are a view, not extra permission: every call still goes through the key's scopes, services, operations, limits, approvals and privacy tier. A write gets its own idempotency key if the app does not send one.

**Meta Muse:** ask Muse to connect a remote MCP server at `https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp?tools=operations`, authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer `. Give it a key with only the services it should use. Muse keeps the key in its own credential store.

sections.heading: HivePunkz and other NFT agents
sections.text:
The `nft-agents` service lets Grok Bot, a Muse or any agent with a key use the person's own NFT agents: HivePunkz, Loopers, JPEG Frens and any other NFT that is an agent. Search for `nft-agents` to find its actions.

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `agents.list` | The agents in the wallet the person linked on hivemindos.app/chat, each with an id like `hivepunkz:441`. |
| `agents.get` | Any bee or agent NFT: its card, shift, holder and what its holder shares. Free. |
| `agents.chat` | Talk with one of the person's own agents in its own voice. The linked wallet must hold it. Billed as the model costs. |
| `bees.quote`, `bees.run`, `bees.job` | Talk to or hire someone else's shared bee. Quote, ask the person, then run on exactly the quoted price. |
| `bees.services.list`, `bees.services.set` | See and set what one of your own bees sells. Service `writing` with a `priceUsd` turns paid writing on with nothing to approve onchain; any other service is repriced or switched. The linked wallet must hold the bee. |
| `agents.open` | Set who can talk with one of the person's Loopers, JPEG Frens or other agent NFTs and what it costs. Free until they set a fee (`mode`, `freeUses`, `feeCredits` up to 50, `feePercent` up to 25%). |
| `agents.policy` | Read an agent's rule before talking with it. |
| `agents.ask` | Talk with someone else's agent: its own free chat if it has one, otherwise in its voice on the person's free replies, then credits, plus its holder's fee only if one is set. |
| `agents.earnings`, `agents.claim` | What the person's opened agents have earned, and claiming it into their credits. See [rewards](rewards.html). |

A chat never runs work for the agent. When an agent asks for something to be done, the answer includes it as `work`, and your agent runs it only if the person agrees and the key allows it.

sections.heading: Rules to give the agent
sections.text:
1. Search before every unfamiliar action. Never invent an `actionId`.
2. Use `hive_read` for actions marked `read` and `hive_write` for `write` or `execute`.
3. Reuse an idempotency key only for the same intended write and the same input.
4. Ask the user before payments, trades, transfers, signatures, deletion, publishing, or any other consequential action.
5. Never send a seed phrase, wallet private key, API secret, or unrelated credential as service input.
6. Treat an approval request or HTTP 402 response as a pause for user confirmation, not permission to continue.

The [SuperAgent API skill](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/SKILL.md) includes these rules and the full setup workflow.

sections.heading: Projects, files, and payments
sections.text:
- A project-bound key always stays in its project. An account-level key can pick a project with the protected `X-HivemindOS-Project` header or the `projectId` tool argument.
- JSON actions return their normal API result. Binary downloads return an authenticated resource link; fetch it with the same key. Binary uploads take `bodyBase64` plus a file header such as `X-File-Name`.
- MCP calls use the same Agent Credit balance, pricing, limits, approvals, and audit trail as REST and the SDK.
- To buy Agent Credits with x402, search for `credits.x402.topUp` and call it with `hive_write`. The first call returns the payment challenge. After the user confirms the exact amount, the x402 wallet signs and the retry sends `Payment-Signature` with the same idempotency key. The MCP cannot change the recipient, network, asset, price, or credited account.

sections.heading: Protocol details
sections.text:
The endpoint is a stateless Streamable HTTP MCP server. It supports `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, notifications, and JSON-RPC batches. Tool annotations mark read-only and consequential actions. `GET /v1/actions` publishes the same key-filtered action catalog over REST for SDK clients and custom adapters.

Every call goes through the normal SuperAgent API request path, so MCP adds no second permission system.

For GPU-marketplace-only agents there is also a separate [Hive Compute MCP](compute-faucet.html#connect-an-agent-through-mcp).

# Managed memory and knowledge

Cloud Superbrain (`cloud-superbrain`) lets a hosted app remember useful context between calls. It saves facts and decisions, finds them by words or meaning, answers from them with citations, and keeps earlier versions when something changes.

Each HivemindOS account gets an isolated memory store; no desktop session or Obsidian vault is needed. A project-bound key, or a request for one of your app's end users, gets a brain of its own inside the account, sharing the account's plan and allowance. See [one brain per project or user](#one-brain-per-project-or-user). Use the local [Hive Superbrain](https://hivemindos.app/docs/for-users/whole-brain/brain-services.html) instead when a user's Obsidian vault should stay the editable source of truth.

sections.heading: Costs
sections.text:
| Mode | Operation | Result | Charge |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Lexical search | `memory.search` | Fast matches from titles, content, tags, projects, entities, aliases, and usage. | 0 credits |
| Semantic recall | `memory.recall` | Hybrid meaning and keyword matches, with the evidence used for ranking. Add `rerank: true` to have the best 20 read again against the question. | 1 credit |
| Memory Answer | `memory.answer` | A concise answer grounded in returned memories, plus cited memory ids. Add `stream: true` to get it as it is written. | 5 credits with the default reader |
| Erase an end user | `memory.erase` | Everything one of your app's end users has in memory, gone in one call. | 0 credits |

Semantic Recall and Memory Answer are paid per use from the account's credits; no plan is needed. Lexical search, storage within the plan, history, graph reads, capsules, and health checks use no agent credits. Call `catalog.get` when onboarding an account to show its plan, storage limits, and availability.

Indexing runs when memory changes, so there is no idle charge. A new memory is searchable by keyword at once and joins Semantic Recall when its index status is ready; `memory.health` reports that state.

sections.heading: Save a memory
sections.text:
Only `title` and `contentText` are required. Add a stable `memoryKey` when later calls should update one subject instead of creating new records.

```ts
const saved = await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "cloud-superbrain",
 "memory.create",
 {
 title: "Aurora compute funding decision",
 contentText: "Compute capacity starts only after the customer-funded job is accepted.",
 memoryKey: "decision:aurora-compute-funding",
 memoryType: "decision",
 project: "Aurora",
 confidence: 0.96,
 tags: ["compute", "commercial"],
 entities: ["Project Aurora", "Hive Compute"],
 evidenceCount: 3,
 },
 { idempotencyKey: "aurora-compute-decision-v1" },
);

if (!saved.ok) throw new Error(saved.error);
const memoryId = saved.result.memory.id;
```

- Memory types: `instruction`, `fact`, `decision`, `goal`, `commitment`, `preference`, `relationship`, `context`, `event`, `learning`, `observation`, `artifact`, `error`, `action`, and `knowledge`.
- Optional fields: `path`, `kind`, `mimeType`, `mediaUrl`, `links`, `metaTags`, `aliases`, `sourceType`, `actorRole`, `memoryOrigin`, and `cognitiveStage`.
- `memory.batch` saves up to 25 records; each returns its own id and generation receipt.
- `occurredAt` dates a memory written after the fact, such as one you import from another system: `"2026-09-25"` or a full ISO time like `"2026-09-25T14:30:00Z"`. Recall ranks the memory by it, and Memory Answer shows the reader that date instead of the day you saved it, so "my driving test is tomorrow", said on the 25th and imported on the 30th, is not read as still to come. It cannot be in the future (a clock up to five minutes fast is allowed) or before 1900; either is refused with 400. Every memory returns `occurredAt`, or `null` when it is dated by when it was written. `memory.update` keeps it unless you send a new one (`null` clears it); `memory.evolve` dates the new version now unless you pass one; `capsules.import` keeps each memory's original time.
- Content that looks like a credential, private key, bearer token, seed phrase, or mnemonic is rejected. Store the credential's name and whether it is set, and keep the value in a secret manager.

sections.heading: Search and answer
Stream the answer
Choose who reads the answer
Past conversations
sections.text:
Save a chat transcript as a memory and recall reads it exchange by exchange. A memory is read as a transcript when its turns are marked `**User:**` and `**Assistant:**` (or an agent's name), or when its lines start with `User:` and `Assistant:`. Put the conversation's date in the frontmatter as `startedAt` or `date`; otherwise the save date is used.

```ts
await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "cloud-superbrain",
 "memory.create",
 {
 title: "Support chat with Dana",
 path: "Conversations/2026-09-14-dana.md",
 contentText: [
 "---",
 "startedAt: 2026-09-14T15:02:00Z",
 "---",
 "User: The replacement blender arrived cracked, same as the first one.",
 "Assistant: Sorry about that. I've refunded the second order to the original card.",
 ].join("\n"),
 },
 { idempotencyKey: "support-chat-dana-0914" },
);
```

When a search or recall returns a transcript, the response also carries `conversationEvidence`: the best-matching exchanges across the account's transcripts, oldest first under each conversation's date. `conversationEvidenceMemoryIds` names their memories.

| Field | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `evidenceChars` | 4,200 | The size of `conversationEvidence`, from 1,000 to 24,000 characters. |
| `evidence` | On, except at `detail: "abstract"` | `false` leaves the exchanges out; `true` adds them at any detail tier. |

Memory Answer reads the same exchanges plus the best part of every other supporting memory, and knows today's date, so "how long ago" and "which came first" questions work. If the conversations fit, it reads them whole. If not, and you pass `turbo: true`, the Turbo decision model orders the exchanges by how likely each is to hold the answer, and the answer reads excerpts from the best 12,000 characters. The decision model is not private, so it is used only when every exchange was written in the standard tier, and never for a private answer. Turbo also reads the best 20 candidate memories again against the question before choosing which conversations to read, the same second read as `rerank: true` in recall. Both run at a third-party model provider (OpenRouter): the question, the exchanges, and the candidate memories' text are sent to it under its own terms. Turbo is off unless you pass `turbo: true` (since 2026-09-29); without it the answer keeps keyword order and sends nothing to that provider. The response's `turbo` says whether it ran. The response's `evidenceOrder` says which order was used (`keyword` when conversations were read whole). Neither choice changes the price.

sections.heading: One brain per project or user
sections.text:
When a request is made with a project-bound key, with `X-HivemindOS-Project`, or for one of your app's end users (`X-HivemindOS-End-User`, or a key bound with `endUserId`), Cloud Superbrain reads and writes a separate brain for that project, that end user, or that end user within that project:

- It starts empty and never sees the account's own memories, or a desktop brain synced to them. The account's own requests never see it.
- Ids, memory keys, history, and search stay inside it. An id from another brain is not found.
- It uses the account's plan. Every brain in the account shares the plan's one allowance.
- Buying a plan and syncing a desktop brain need an account-level request; a scoped request is refused.

See [projects and isolation](projects-security.html#act-for-one-of-your-apps-users) for how to name an end user.

sections.heading: Erase an end user's memory
Ask for only as much as you need
sections.text:
Recall returns whole memories by default. Pass `detail` to get less:

| `detail` | Each hit carries | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| `abstract` | Id, title, type, project, status, updated date, score, and a one-line excerpt. | Surveying candidates, then re-requesting the few that matter. |
| `overview` | The full metadata record, ranked excerpt, and score details — no body. | Ranking and filtering when the body is not needed yet. |
| `full` | Everything, including `contentText`. **The default.** | Reading the memory. |

```ts
const survey = await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "cloud-superbrain",
 "memory.recall",
 { query: "Who pays before an Aurora GPU starts?", mode: "hybrid", detail: "abstract", limit: 8 },
 { idempotencyKey: "aurora-memory-survey-001" },
);
```

`detail` only trims the response. It never changes which memories rank, their order, what `memory.answer` is grounded on, or the price. The response echoes the `detail` it applied.

sections.heading: Change, replace, or delete a memory
Maintenance and history
sections.text:
- **Find duplicates:** `memory.consolidate` groups near-duplicates within a memory type, spots memories that say they correct an earlier note but were written without `supersedes`, and lists aged-out memories nothing has retrieved. It reports rather than merges: each group comes with the exact `memory.evolve` call to review. With `applyArchives: true` it archives aged-out candidates (reversible, and only `context`, `event`, `observation`, and `action` memories older than 120 days with no retrieval history). `memory.health` also reports `duplicatePressure` for scheduled checks.
- **Learn from what agents did:** `memory.minePatterns` reads operational memories and proposes recurring failures, workflows worth turning into a skill, and operations stable enough to schedule. Test traffic and retries of one task are not counted. It never creates anything; send a candidate to `memory.create` to keep it.
- **Browse by path:** `memory.browse` summarizes path groups without bodies (about 100 tokens per group at `abstract`, about 2,000 at `overview`). `memory.recall` with `mode: "hierarchical"` scores groups first, so a memory's neighbours come back with it. Hierarchy only changes order; it never hides a memory.
- **Replay history:** each write publishes an immutable generation. `generations.list` reads retained generations and the replay boundary; `generations.compare` shows added, removed, and changed ids between two. `memory.recall` with `generationId` replays a lexical question against an old state; `temporalMode: "historical"` includes superseded and archived records, and `temporalMode: "as-of"` with `asOf` sets a time cutoff. Up to 256 generations are kept per account. A request outside the replay boundary fails rather than using newer memory.
- **Knowledge graph:** memories with type `knowledge`, a `knowledge` tag, or a path under `Synthesis/` become knowledge nodes. Use `knowledge.search`, `knowledge.get`, `knowledge.backlinks` (connections through entities, aliases, and links), and `knowledge.graph` (a bounded node-and-edge view). Use `entities`, `aliases`, and `links` consistently for dependable navigation.
- **Portable capsules:** `capsules.export` returns a checksummed capsule of selected memories or the next page of the account; export at most 100 memories per part and follow `hasMore` and `nextCursor`. `capsules.import` checks the schema and hash before adding records to the authenticated account; it can never grant access to the source account or overwrite another account's memory. `capsules.open`, `capsules.search`, and `capsules.preview` inspect a capsule and report what an import would change without writing anything; a damaged capsule is still shown, with a warning. The checksum detects corruption but is not encryption, so keep private capsules private.

# Pay per call with x402

An agent with an x402 wallet on Base can use the SuperAgent API without an account or API key. It pays for one call at a time in USDC, and only when the call succeeds. It can also pay once for an account and get an API key holding the credits.

sections.heading: Make a call
sections.text:
Send the operation's input as the body:

```http
POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/x402/svg-studio/svgs.generate
Content-Type: application/json

{ "prompt": "Minimal flat bee logo, black and honey-yellow" }
```

1. The first answer is HTTP 402 with a `Payment-Required` header, priced from your input. If the input is wrong, you get HTTP 400 instead, before any payment is asked for.
2. Show the person the exact amount and get their approval. Then send the same request again with `Payment-Signature`. Any x402 v2 client does this step for you.
3. The call runs. On success the payment settles and you get the result, with an `x402` block holding the receipt id and transaction. On failure you get `x402.charged: false` and the payment is never taken, so you can try the same payment again.

Sending the same signed payment again within 30 minutes returns the same answer. The call does not run twice and you are not charged twice.

sections.heading: What you can buy
sections.text:
`GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/x402` lists every operation for sale, with its price, address, an example input and the input's schema. No key is needed. Today it covers:

| Service | Operations |
|---|---|
| Hive Research | Token research at Scout, Swarm or Superbrain depth |
| Token Autopsy | Standard and panel token reports |
| Wallet Risk | A risk snapshot of a wallet |
| Reddit VOC | Snapshot and deep voice-of-customer reports |
| Swarm | Quick and Theater scenario runs |
| X Studio | Style skills and engagement audits of an X account |
| MiroShark | Crowd simulations |
| Testnet faucet | Testnet gas and test stablecoins |
| Media Studio | Images and video |
| Photo Keyworder | Keywords, title and description for a photo |
| SVG Studio | Vectorize, generate, edit and animate SVGs |
| Lead-gen data | Find local businesses, and enrich them |

A call costs what the same operation costs an account with no HIVE stake. The price comes from the service when you call, so it is never out of date.

sections.heading: Collect a background result
sections.text:
Research, reports, swarms, simulations and media run in the background. Their answer includes `followUp.apiKey`, an API key that can use only that service and can never move funds. Store it like any secret and use it to read the result:

```http
POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/services/token-autopsy/invoke
Authorization: Bearer 
Idempotency-Key: 
Content-Type: application/json

{ "operationId": "reports.get", "pathParameters": { "reportId": " " } }
```

If a call uses less than it was priced at, the difference stays on the same key as Agent Credits.

sections.heading: Buy an account instead
sections.text:
Sites, agents, workflows, databases, wallets, trading, subscriptions and connected accounts keep running or belong to an account, so they are not sold per call. Buy an account for those:

```http
POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/x402/accounts
Content-Type: application/json

{ "amountUsd": 5 }
```

After the same 402 and `Payment-Signature` steps, you get an API key holding that many Agent Credits (500 per dollar, from $1 to $500) for every service. Save it as `HIVEMINDOS_API_KEY`. It can never move funds. Manage the account later in the [console](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/console/).

sections.heading: Private tiers
sections.text: The same routes work under `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/private/x402` and `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/confidential/x402`, where only operations that meet the tier are sold. See [privacy tiers](privacy.html).

sections.heading: Rules for agents
sections.text:
- A 402 answer is a price, not permission. Ask the person to approve the exact amount before a wallet signs.
- Never send a wallet's private key or recovery phrase to HivemindOS. The payment is a signature the wallet makes itself.
- HivemindOS sets the recipient, network, asset and price on its server. Do not try to change them.

sections.heading: Find it in the x402 Bazaar
sections.text: Every route describes its input and output for the Coinbase x402 Bazaar, so agents that search the Bazaar can find it. A route appears there after its first paid call.

# Private and confidential access

The SuperAgent API has three base URLs. They are the same API with the same paths; each offers only what meets its privacy level.

- Fine with any model or service? Use `/v1`.
- What you send must never reach a service that keeps it? Use `/v1/private`.
- Models must also run in hardware that proves what it runs? Use `/v1/confidential`.

| Tier | Base URL | Remote MCP | What it offers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1` | `https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp` | Every model and service. Providers may keep what you send under their own terms. |
| Private | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/private` | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/private/mcp` | Only models and services that keep nothing you send. |
| Confidential | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/confidential` | `https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/confidential/mcp` | Private, and models run in attested hardware that proves what it runs on every request. |

Swap `/v1` for the tier's base in any path: `/v1/private/services/cloud-superbrain/invoke` is the private version of `/v1/services/cloud-superbrain/invoke`.

sections.heading: What each tier includes
sections.text:
The catalog, capabilities, actions, MCP tools and OpenAPI document under a tier's base list only what that tier includes, so read them from the base you will call:

```http
GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/private/catalog
```

Each capability's `privacy` field shows the strictest tier it serves.

| Included in | Examples |
|---|---|
| Every tier | Your account, projects, API keys, usage, files, connections, managed databases, analytics, app hosting, wallets, trading, swaps, bridge quotes, runs, approvals, webhooks, and model lists. Memory writes, reads, keyword search and recall. Chat (`managed-models`) and Memory Answer, with only the models that meet the tier. |
| Private and standard | Semantic Recall and memory index rebuilds, which use HivemindOS's own models, and media generation, which in the private tier offers only the private media models. |
| Standard only | Web search and research, X, email, social publishing, lead data, managed agents, request classification, and plain-language routing and planning. Each sends what you give it to a service that may keep it. |

Memory saved in the standard tier can also leave HivemindOS: recall's `rerank: true` and Memory Answer's Turbo ordering send the question and standard-tier memory text to a third-party model provider (OpenRouter), under its own terms. Memories saved in the private or confidential tier are never sent. See [managed memory](memory.html#search-and-answer).

Hive Compute serves every tier. Under the private and confidential bases it runs only on hosts with fresh verified hardware attestation, whatever the request's own `privacy` setting says.

In the confidential tier:

- **Chat and Memory Answer** use only models that run in an attested enclave, checked on every request. A reply without that check is discarded and not charged.
- **Memory Answer** has no default reader, because the default is private but not attested. Name one from `memory.models` under the confidential base as `model`.
- **Memories** are never sent to an embedding model. Recall finds them by keyword, so Semantic Recall is refused with `409`.
- **Media** models are listed and jobs can be read, but nothing is generated: no media model runs in attested hardware yet.

sections.heading: Models
sections.text:
Every model in the managed catalog has a `privacy_level`: `standard`, `private` or `confidential`. Under a tier's base, `managed-models` `models.list` returns only models that meet it, and a chat naming any other model is refused before anything is charged.

- `private`: the provider publishes that it keeps no prompts or replies, or HivemindOS runs the model.
- `confidential`: also runs in an enclave whose attestation is checked on every request. The provider names these models with a `:private` suffix.
- `standard`: every other model.

Media generation follows the same rule: under the private base, the media catalog and `/media/models` list only private media models.

Memory Answer lets you choose its reader the same way. See [managed memory](memory.html#choose-who-reads-the-answer).

sections.heading: Pin a key to a tier
When something is refused
sections.text:
An operation below the request's tier is refused with `403` before anything runs or is charged:

```json
{
 "ok": false,
 "code": "privacy_tier",
 "privacy": "private",
 "operationPrivacy": "standard",
 "error": "This operation is not available in the private tier: what it is given would reach a service that does not meet it. Use it through /v1, with a key that is not pinned to a tier."
}
```

In the private tiers, name managed operations by `operationId`. A raw service path that is not a published operation cannot be checked, so it is refused.

sections.heading: What HivemindOS keeps
sections.text:
- A reply from a private model is kept for 15 minutes, so a retry with the same idempotency key, or a recovery lookup, can still collect it after a dropped connection. Then the words are deleted and only the billing record stays. A later retry is told the reply is gone; it never runs the model or charges again.
- What you ask HivemindOS to store is kept as usual: memories, files, database records, and saved run results.
- A memory keeps the strictest tier it was written in. Memory Answer reads it only with a reader that meets that tier.
- A run keeps the tier it was created in. An idempotency key used in one tier cannot be reused in another.
