# Projects, isolation, and service accounts

A project keeps one product, customer, or environment separate from another. Its wallets, approvals, runs, files, webhooks, database data, usage, and audit history stay inside it. Inside an account or a project, an end user id keeps each of your app's own users apart as well.

Use projects when you have more than one customer, app, or environment. For a small first integration, the account-level default is enough.

sections.heading: Create a project
Give each workload its own key
sections.text:
Create a child key with `projectId`. The project binding can never be removed or changed, and every descendant inherits it.

```ts
const worker = await hive.apiKeys.create(
 {
 label: "Acme research worker",
 projectId,
 scopes: [
 "services:read",
 "services:invoke",
 "runs:read",
 "runs:write",
 "artifacts:read",
 ],
 allowedServices: ["hive-research"],
 allowedOperations: [
 "capabilities.list",
 "services.invoke.hive-research.analyses.create",
 "runs.create.hive-research.analyses.create",
 "runs.read",
 "artifacts.list",
 "artifacts.content.read",
 ],
 },
 { idempotencyKey: "key-acme-research-worker-v1" },
);
```

This is the recommended service-account pattern: one project-bound key per workload, with exact scopes, services, operations, expiry, and limits.

sections.heading: Pick a project with an account key
sections.text:
An account-level key can select an active project for one request:

```http
X-HivemindOS-Project: project_...
```

The TypeScript client sends that header for you when created with `projectId`:

```ts
const acme = new HivemindOSClient({
 apiKey: process.env.HIVEMINDOS_ACCOUNT_API_KEY!,
 projectId: "project_...",
});
```

A project-bound key rejects a different project header. Use one client per project, and never pass an unchecked project id straight from an end-user request.

sections.heading: Act for one of your app's users
sections.text:
When your app serves its own users, name the user a request is for, so what a service stores for one of them never reaches another. An account-level or project key sends the id on each request:

```http
X-HivemindOS-End-User: user_8f2c41
```

Or bind a key to one end user when you create it, with `endUserId`:

```ts
const userKey = await hive.apiKeys.create(
 {
 label: "Memory for user_8f2c41",
 projectId,
 endUserId: "user_8f2c41",
 scopes: ["services:read", "services:invoke"],
 allowedServices: ["cloud-superbrain"],
 },
 { idempotencyKey: "key-user_8f2c41-memory-v1" },
);
```

- An end user id is 1–128 characters: letters, digits, and `.` `_` `:` `@` `-`, starting with a letter or digit. Use your own stable, opaque user id, and set it in your backend from the signed-in user, never from a value the user can edit.
- The binding is permanent. Every child key inherits it, a bound key cannot name a different end user (`403`), and a request's `X-HivemindOS-End-User` must match the key's binding.
- Runs remember the end user they were created for.
- Keys report the binding in `endUserId`.

sections.heading: Which services keep a project or user apart
sections.text:
A project-bound key, an `X-HivemindOS-Project` header, or an `X-HivemindOS-End-User` header promises that one project's or one user's data stays apart. The services below keep that promise: a project or end user sees and changes only what it created, never the account's own data or another user's. Plans, allowances, limits and charges stay the account's, so every project and end user draws on the same balance and counts toward the same plan limits.

| Keeps apart | Services |
|---|---|
| Each project and each end user | `cloud-superbrain`, `hive-research`, `swarm`, `x-studio`, `x-transcript`, `reddit-voc`, `media-studio`, `token-autopsy`, `wallet-risk`, `outbound-email`, `hivemind-finance`, `managed-bookings`, `managed-socials`, `hivemind-analytics`, `svg-studio`, `photo-keyworder`, `distill`, `gpu-rentals`, `integration-broker`, `managed-agents`, `managed-workflows`, `copy-trading`, `managed-media`, `miroshark`, `hiveverse`, `hive-compute`, `x-api` |
| Each project (no end user yet) | `hivemind-database`, `managed-wallets`, `managed-trading`, `universal-swaps` |
| Nothing to keep apart: it stores nothing a later call can read back, so any key may use it | `answer-engine`, `managed-models`, `leadgen-data`, `web-data`, `onchain-intelligence`, `hive-bridge`, `testnet-faucet`, `hall` |
| The whole account only | `app-hosting`, `nft-agents` (except `agents.get` and `agents.policy`), `agent-service-access` (except `plans.list`), and the Copy wallet routes of `copy-trading` |

The last row belongs to the account as a whole: an account's hosted sites, its wallet's NFT agents and their earnings, its prepaid service access, and money held in its Copy wallet. A project or end-user request to one of them is refused before anything runs or is charged, for managed-service calls and runs alike:

```json
{
 "ok": false,
 "code": "scope_not_supported",
 "serviceId": "app-hosting",
 "error": "This managed service does not keep one project's data apart from the rest of the account yet, so a project-bound key cannot use it. Use an account-level key."
}
```

Call these with an account-level key and no end user, and keep your own users' data apart in your backend.

On `managed-bookings`, each plan allows one booking profile per account, whichever project or end user sets it up first.

**Memory.** In Cloud Superbrain, each project, each end user, and each end user within a project gets a brain of its own. It starts empty, never includes the account's own memories (or a desktop brain synced to them), and uses the account's plan: every brain in the account shares the one plan's storage and allowance. Plans are bought, and a desktop brain synced, with an account-level request. See [managed memory](memory.html).

sections.heading: Isolation rules
sections.text:
- Resource ids only mean something inside their account and project. An id from one project returns not found from another.
- Idempotency keys are isolated by project and API key.
- Webhooks receive only events from their project and allowed services.
- Usage and audit queries report only the selected project.
- Managed databases follow the same project boundary.
- A project-bound key cannot create another project or an account-level child key.
- A managed service that cannot keep a project or end user apart refuses the request with `scope_not_supported` instead of serving account-wide data. See [which services keep a project or user apart](#which-services-keep-a-project-or-user-apart).

sections.heading: Separate your environments
sections.text: Create separate projects, API keys, and webhook destinations for development, staging, and production. Do not run tests in a production project: isolation protects data, but it cannot tell that a valid production key was used by mistake.

# SuperAgent API reference

The complete map of scopes, endpoints, headers, and limit selectors. For your first call, start with the [quickstart](./).

The [OpenAPI 3.1 document](https://api.hivemindos.app/openapi.json) is the source of truth for request and response shapes, and can generate clients, validators, and API explorers.

```text
Base URL: https://api.hivemindos.app/v1
MCP URL: https://api.hivemindos.app/mcp
Authentication: Authorization: Bearer hmos_live_...
Content type: application/json
```

Database archive parts and downloads use `application/zip` instead of JSON.

sections.heading: What a call costs before you make it
sections.text:
`price.kind` from `/inspect` is one of:

- `free`: the service charges nothing for it.
- `maximum`: the most it can cost, in `credits` and `usd`, for the example or the input you sent. It may cost less.
- `quote`: the service prices it with a free quote first; `quoteOperation` names it.
- `metered`: the service charges what the work cost after it runs, so nothing can say beforehand.
- `unavailable`: the price could not be read just now.

Send `maxCredits` in an invoke body (or the `X-HivemindOS-Max-Credits` header) to hold a call to a ceiling. It runs only when its price is known up front to fit; otherwise it is refused with HTTP 409 and nothing is charged: `price_above_maximum` (with `priceCredits`) or `price_not_known_up_front`. A key's `creditsPerCall` limit does the same for every call it makes, and the lower of the two decides. See [limits](limits.html#most-one-call-may-cost).

sections.heading: When an answer never arrived
sections.text:
`GET /requests/outcome?idempotencyKey= ` reads what became of that request, without running or charging anything:

| `state` | What to do |
|---|---|
| `none` | Nothing is running or kept under that key. Send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key`: what a service already did under it is not done twice. |
| `in_progress` | It is still running. Wait and check again; never resend it with a new key. |
| `completed` | It finished. Send it again with the same key and body to get the stored answer, charged nothing. `chargedCredits` says what it cost. |
| `interrupted` | It stopped before its result was recorded and may have been charged. Look for it in `GET /usage` before sending the work again with a new key. |

sections.heading: x402 Agent Credit top-up
sections.text:
Send `{ "amountUsd": 5 }` to `POST /credits/x402/top-up` with an API key that has `credits:write`, an `Idempotency-Key`, and access to `credits.x402.topUp`. Amounts may be $5 to $500 with no more than two decimal places.

The first request returns HTTP 402 and `Payment-Required`. An x402 v2 client signs the exact Base payment and retries the same request with `Payment-Signature` and the same idempotency key. A successful response includes `creditedUsd`, `creditedCredits`, `receiptId`, and the updated `credits` balance.

The route never accepts a recipient, network, asset, price, credit token, or alternate account in its body. Those values are fixed and verified by HivemindOS, and the payment settles to the same official HivemindOS revenue wallet used by the other managed x402 services.

sections.heading: Deprecation policy
sections.text:
New operations and response fields can be added at any time, so ignore fields you do not know. Before an operation is removed or changed incompatibly:

- It is marked deprecated in the public changelog, with what to use instead, at least 30 days before it stops working.
- Responses from it carry a `Deprecation` header, and a `Sunset` header with the date it stops working, for that whole period.
- It keeps working until the `Sunset` date.

Watch for the `Deprecation` header in your logs, so a removal never comes as a surprise.

# Rewards and the Hall

The SuperAgent API pays you back for real use. What your apps and agents earn is sent to your wallet in USDC on Base on its own once it reaches $5, paid from the revenue those calls brought in; you can claim it as Agent Credits (500 to the dollar) any time instead. Bonuses and bounties pay in Agent Credits, and receipts earn Honey. Nothing pays for minting.

- **[Rewards](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/rewards/)** lists every program with its rule and a button to act on it.
- **[The Hall](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/hall/)** shows this week's most-paid agents, collections and apps, ranked by how many different accounts paid for them, then by calls. A holder talking with their own agent, or an app's owner using their own app, doesn't count.

Agents can read the Hall with no key:

```http
GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/hall
GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/hall?week=2026-09-28
GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/hall/bounties
GET https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/hall/receipts/{receiptId}
```

A week runs Monday to Sunday in UTC and is named by its Monday.

sections.heading: Your first payment, matched
sections.text:
The first time you pay over x402, to [buy an account](pay-per-call.html) or [top up credits](reference.html#x402-agent-credit-top-up), we add twice what you paid in Agent Credits, up to 1,000 credits ($2). A $1 account holds $3. It applies once per paying wallet and once per account, and up to 50 matches a week.

The response shows the match as `firstPaymentBonusCredits`, with a `rewards` link to the full list.

sections.heading: Receipts
sections.text:
Every charged response carries two headers:

| Header | What it is |
|---|---|
| `X-HivemindOS-Receipt-Id` | The call's receipt id |
| `X-HivemindOS-Receipt-Url` | The receipt's page on hivemindos.app |

A receipt is private until the person who paid makes it public, from the receipt's page or from Rewards. A public receipt shows the service, the operation, the price and when it was paid, never who paid.

Making a receipt public earns **5 Honey**, up to 3 receipts a week, for calls of 5 credits or more from the last 7 days. Honey is your lifetime contribution record on HivemindOS. It is never exchanged for HIVE and can't be sold or cashed out.

sections.heading: Your app earns 5%
sections.text:
Register your app on [Rewards](https://hivemindos.app/superagent-api/rewards/) to get an app id, then send it with every call your app makes:

```http
X-HivemindOS-App: app_0123456789ab
```

You earn 5% of the credits other accounts spend through your app, up to 25,000 credits a week per app, sent to your linked wallet in USDC on Base on their own once they reach $5, or claimed as Agent Credits any time. Your own calls don't count, and neither do wallet, swap, trading, credit or top-up calls. Your app also shows on the Hall. An account can register up to 5 apps.

The header works on keyed calls, runs, MCP and [pay per call](pay-per-call.html).

sections.heading: Your agent earns your fee
sections.text:
Anyone can talk with your Looper, JPEG Fren or any other agent NFT, free. If you like, charge a fee on each reply: a flat amount (up to 50 credits), a share of what the reply costs (up to 25%), or both, optionally after a few free replies each day. If your agent publishes its own chat, people reach that; otherwise it speaks in its own voice from its onchain persona. What it earns is sent to the holding wallet in USDC on Base on its own once it reaches $5, or can be claimed as Agent Credits any time.

They're operations of the `nft-agents` service, so an agent finds them through [MCP](mcp.html) or calls them with `POST /v1/services/nft-agents/invoke`:

| Operation | What it does | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `agents.open` | Set who can talk with your agent and what it costs | `{ "agent": "looper:12", "mode": "quota", "freeUses": 5, "feeCredits": 1 }` |
| `agents.policy` | Read any agent's rule before talking with it | `?agent=looper:12` |
| `agents.ask` | Talk with someone else's opened agent | `{ "agent": "looper:12", "message": "..." }` |
| `agents.earnings` | What your agents have earned | none |
| `agents.claim` | Claim it as Agent Credits, or as USDC with `as: "usdc"` | none, or `{ "as": "usdc" }` |

```http
POST https://api.hivemindos.app/v1/services/nft-agents/invoke
Authorization: Bearer hmos_live_...
Idempotency-Key: ask-looper-12-0001
Content-Type: application/json

{ "operationId": "agents.ask", "input": { "agent": "looper:12", "message": "What do you do?" } }
```

Payouts go out within minutes of reaching $5, up to $100 at a time; anything above follows on the next run. `{ "as": "usdc" }` on `agents.claim` or `apps.claim` sends a balance of $5 or more right away instead of waiting.

Only the wallet that holds the NFT can set its rule, and the rule resets if the NFT changes hands. `mode` is free, quota (`freeUses` free replies each day or month, then the fee) or paid; send only what you change. A reply from `agents.ask` costs nothing extra when there's no fee: the agent's own free chat, or your free Swarm Scout replies, then credits. When a fee applies, the person asking needs about 50 spare credits while it runs. HivePunkz are shared from their own card instead, with `bees.quote` and `bees.run`. You can also open an agent from its settings on [hivemindos.app/agents](https://hivemindos.app/agents/).

# Runs, artifacts, webhooks, and errors

Use a **direct call** when your app can wait for the answer. Use a **run** when work may continue after the request ends; its result is saved as an **artifact**. Use a **webhook** when HivemindOS should tell your app that something changed.

Event format

```http
X-HivemindOS-Event: run.succeeded
X-HivemindOS-Delivery: delivery_...
X-HivemindOS-Signature: t=1787551200,v1= 
Content-Type: application/json
```


Current events:

- `run.started`, `run.succeeded`, and `run.failed`
- `approval.created`, `approval.approved`, and `approval.rejected`

sections.heading: Verify a signature
Error envelope
sections.text:
Every JSON error has `ok: false` and a customer-safe `error`. Some add fields that tell your app what to do next.

| HTTP | Meaning | What to do |
|---:|---|---|
| 400 | The request shape or value is invalid. | Fix the request; do not repeat it unchanged. |
| 401 | The key is invalid, revoked, or expired. | Stop using it and rotate credentials. |
| 402 | The HivemindOS credit balance or managed database allowance is insufficient. | Ask the account owner to top up, activate an eligible plan, or reduce usage. |
| 403 | The key scope, service boundary, delegated authority, approval, or wallet policy rejects the action. | Use a suitably restricted key or change the account-owned policy through its normal review path. |
| 404 | The route or account-owned resource was not found. | Check the id and the key's service boundary. |
| 409 | The state, confirmation, quote, approval, or idempotency key conflicts with the request. | Read the current resource. Use a fresh quote or idempotency key only for a genuinely new action. |
| 410 | A downloadable database archive expired. | Start a new download copy. |
| 413 | The request or upload part is too large. | Reduce or split the input within the documented limits. |
| 424 | Required managed-service setup is incomplete. | Ask the account owner to finish setup first. |
| 429 | An API-key limit was reached. | Wait for `retryAfterSeconds` and respect `Retry-After`. See [limits](limits.html#handle-http-429). |
| 500 | Something failed inside HivemindOS. | Keep the same idempotency key and retry with bounded backoff when the action is safe to repeat. |
| 502, 503, 504 | A managed service failed, was unavailable, or did not answer in time. See [managed service calls](#managed-service-calls). | Retry with the same idempotency key, after `Retry-After` when present. |

A few `code` values worth handling on their own:

| `code` | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `scope_not_supported` | 403 | The service cannot keep a project or end user apart, so it refuses a project-bound key or a project or end-user request. See [projects and isolation](projects-security.html#which-services-keep-a-project-or-user-apart). |
| `approval_requires_another_principal` | 403 | The approval came from the key that asked for it or from a key in its family. |
| `approval_consumed` | 409 | The approval was already used, or is being used by a request still in flight. Ask for a new approval for a new action. |

sections.heading: Managed service calls
sections.text:
A call through `POST /services/{serviceId}/invoke` reports the service's own answer in a stable envelope:

```json
{
 "ok": false,
 "serviceId": "hive-research",
 "operationId": "analyses.create",
 "status": 503,
 "upstreamStatus": 503,
 "code": "upstream_unavailable",
 "error": "The service is busy. Try again shortly.",
 "retryAfterSeconds": 30,
 "chargedCredits": 0,
 "result": {}
}
```

`status` is the HTTP status of this response; `upstreamStatus` is the status the service itself returned.

| HTTP | `code` | Meaning | What to do |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 200 | none | The service succeeded. | Use `result`. |
| 4xx | `upstream_rejected`, `payment_required` (402), `rate_limited` (429) | The service refused this input. Its status is passed through. | Fix the request; do not repeat it unchanged. |
| 502 | `upstream_error` | The service failed or answered in a way HivemindOS could not use. | Retry with the same idempotency key and bounded backoff. |
| 503 | `upstream_unavailable` | The service is temporarily unavailable. | Retry after `Retry-After`. |
| 504 | `upstream_timeout` | The service did not answer in time: 60 seconds for most operations, 120 seconds for compute, media, research, and swarm work, 45 seconds for a Memory Answer, and 5 minutes for a streamed reply. | Retry with the same idempotency key. |

When the service says how long to wait, the response carries `Retry-After` and `retryAfterSeconds`. Retrying with the same idempotency key and input is safe: a failed call is not stored, so the retry runs again, and the service is handed the same idempotency key as the first time, so work it already started is not started twice. A retry sent while the first call is still running gets `409`. For a timed-out action that moves money or sends something, you can also read the resource or run first, since the service may have finished after HivemindOS stopped waiting.

sections.heading: Approvals
sections.text:
An approval for a managed action must come from the account owner or from a key outside the requesting key's family: not the requesting key, a key it created, the key that created it, or a sibling. Keep your reviewer key under a separate root key.

Each approval is spent once. The first call that presents it claims it; a second call gets `409` with `approval_consumed`. If the service refuses the input (a 4xx), the approval is given back and can be used again with corrected input.

# Service access and catalog

The service catalog tells you what your key can use and whether it is ready now. Read it before showing a feature or starting work.

sections.heading: List services
sections.text:
```ts
const response = await hive.services.list({ probe: true });
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(response.error);

for (const service of response.services) {
 console.log(service.id, service.status, service.operations);
}
```

The list is already filtered to the key's permissions. Each service has a `status`:

- `available`: ready to use.
- `setup-required`: the account owner must finish setup first.
- `coming-soon` or `unavailable`: do not keep retrying.

Pass `probe: true` when you need a fresh health check from every visible service.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Stable service id used in keys, invocations, runs, events, and limits. |
| `name` and `description` | What the service is for. |
| `category` | `agent`, `app`, `data`, `finance`, `integration`, `media`, or `platform`. |
| `status` | `available`, `setup-required`, `coming-soon`, or `unavailable`. |
| `operations` | Dedicated SuperAgent API routes or the managed-service invocation route. |
| `operationCount` | Number of registered exact capabilities. |
| `capabilitiesUrl` | Filtered capability registry for the service. |

sections.heading: Invoke a service
sections.text:
Most managed services share one route:

```http
POST /v1/services/{serviceId}/invoke
```

Name a stable operation id from `GET /capabilities/{serviceId}` and pass its input. The SDK does this with `invokeOperation`:

```ts
const result = await hive.services.invokeOperation(
 "hive-research",
 "analyses.create",
 { question: "What evidence would falsify this thesis?" },
 { idempotencyKey: "falsify-thesis-001" },
);
```

Over HTTPS, the body looks like this. Path parameters and query values stay separate from `input`:

```json
{
 "operationId": "analyses.get",
 "pathParameters": { "analysisId": "analysis_123" },
 "query": { "includeSources": true }
}
```

Always send an `Idempotency-Key`, even for a read-like operation: the invocation itself is a protected mutation.

The response wraps the service's result:

```json
{
 "ok": true,
 "serviceId": "hive-research",
 "operationId": "analyses.create",
 "status": 200,
 "chargedCredits": 0,
 "result": {
 "ok": true,
 "report": {}
 }
}
```

`chargedCredits` is the exact completed charge reported by the service. It is `0` for free reads and for work that did not complete. The same value is in the `X-HivemindOS-Credits-Charged` header and in usage and audit records.

Good to know:

- An older form with `method` (`DELETE`, `GET`, `PATCH`, `POST`, or `PUT`, default `POST`) and a `path` starting with `/` still works for reviewed paths. Registered operation ids are safer: they validate the method and path, work with exact key access, and stay discoverable.
- Account, payment, credential, administrative, and other private service routes are always rejected.
- Managed databases, wallets, and trading use their own [dedicated endpoints](reference.html#endpoint-map) with narrower scopes.
- For work that should continue after the request ends, create a [durable run](runs-webhooks.html#durable-runs) instead. Direct calls and runs have separate [limit selectors](limits.html#limit-selectors).

# Wallets, approvals, and trading

Managed wallets let your app use a wallet address without ever receiving its private key or recovery phrase. Before money moves, HivemindOS checks the wallet policy, a short-lived quote, the API key's permissions and limits, available Agent Credits, and any required approval.

Every money action follows the same pattern: **quote, approve if needed, then submit once.**

Start on a test network. Move to a main network only after you have tested policy, approval separation, retries, event handling, and recovery end to end.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.text:
Use separate keys for proposing and approving, so a key that can execute an action cannot also approve it. An approval must come from the account owner or from a key outside the requesting key's family: never the key that asked, a key it created, the key that created it, or a sibling (`403` with `approval_requires_another_principal`). Keep the reviewer key under its own root key:

| Responsibility | Suggested scopes |
|---|---|
| Wallet reader | `wallets:read` |
| Wallet creator | `wallets:create`, `wallets:read` |
| Transfer worker | `wallets:read`, `wallets:transact` |
| Message signer | `wallets:read`, `wallets:sign` |
| Trading worker | `wallets:read`, `trading:read`, `trading:execute` |
| Swap worker | `wallets:read`, `wallets:transact` |
| Own-wallet swap builder | `wallets:read` |
| Reviewer | `approvals:read`, `approvals:write` |
| Policy administrator | `wallets:read`, `approvals:write` |

Add `managed-wallets`, `managed-trading`, or `universal-swaps` to each key's service allowlist as needed.

Supported networks: `base`, `base-sepolia`, `ethereum`, `ethereum-sepolia`, `solana`, and `solana-devnet`. Availability may vary, so check `GET /services` and current pricing before offering a network or paid action.

sections.heading: Create a managed wallet
Send a transfer
Sign a message
Place a spot trade
Universal swaps
sections.text:
Universal swaps turn any token into any other, on one chain or across chains. Add `universal-swaps` to the key's service allowlist. Two ways to use it:

- **From a HivemindOS wallet**: quote, approve if the wallet's policy asks, then execute. HivemindOS signs and sends.
- **From your own wallet**: get a checked, unsigned route and sign it yourself. HivemindOS never holds the key.

| Method and path | Scope | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/swaps/tokens` | `wallets:read` | Chains you can swap on and the official token contract each symbol means. Optional `chainId` query. |
| `POST /v1/swaps/quote` | `wallets:transact` | Quote a swap from a HivemindOS wallet. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `POST /v1/swaps` | `wallets:transact` | Execute an approved quote. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `GET /v1/swaps` | `wallets:read` | List swaps. |
| `GET /v1/swaps/{swapId}` | `wallets:read` | Read one swap, with cross-chain fill status. |
| `POST /v1/swaps/prepare` | `wallets:read` | Build an unsigned route for your own wallet. No credits. |
| `GET /v1/swaps/routes/{routeId}` | `wallets:read` | Follow a route your own wallet sent until it fills. |

`GET /v1/swaps/tokens` lists every chain with `canSwapFrom` and `canSwapTo`. `canSwapFrom` refers to HivemindOS wallets, which can start a swap on Base, Ethereum, and Solana; your own wallet can start on any listed chain. A symbol such as `usdc` resolves only to the official contract for that chain. Any other token works when you pass its contract or mint address, and the response flags it as unverified.

**Costs:** an executed swap from a HivemindOS wallet charges 20 Agent Credits, and only when it runs. A 0.45% platform fee is inside the route's price. The quote's `maximumDebitCredits` is the authoritative charge. Routes for your own wallet charge no credits.

A key made from an Agent Credit token cannot hold `wallets:transact`, so it cannot quote or execute swaps from HivemindOS wallets. It can use `POST /v1/swaps/prepare` and `GET /v1/swaps/routes/{routeId}` with `wallets:read`.

sections.heading: Say what to swap
sections.text:
Name the tokens as `chain:symbol`, such as `base:usdc` or `solana:sol`, or as a contract or mint address. Then give one amount:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `amount` | Decimal amount of `from` to spend, such as `"50"`. |
| `amountAtomic` | The same, in the token's smallest unit. |
| `amountOut` | Decimal amount of `to` to receive exactly, such as `"0.8"`. |
| `amountOutAtomic` | The same, in the token's smallest unit. |

Give an amount to spend or an amount to receive, not both. With `amountOut`, the route prices what it costs to receive at least that amount, and `tradeType` comes back as `EXACT_OUTPUT`. Otherwise it is `EXACT_INPUT`.

You can also describe the swap in plain words in `request` and leave the fields out:

- `"swap 50 USDC on Base to SOL"`
- `"i need 0.8 sol"`
- `"swap usdc to 0.8sol"`
- `"move 20 usdc from solana to base"`

- A short, exact sentence like the first one is read directly.
- Anything looser is read the way Ask Scout on the hivemindos.app Trade desk reads it. That uses managed decisions and is billed like any other decision call. A key without `services.invoke.managed-models.decisions.create` gets HTTP 403; use `from`, `to` and an amount instead.
- When the words name no chain, funds start on `defaultChain` (a chain slug, default `base`).
- When they name nothing to pay with, a HivemindOS wallet pays from what it holds, dollars first.

Every quote and route returns `interpretation`: the swap as HivemindOS read it. Show it to the person before anything is spent.

Other optional fields: `slippageBps` (0 to 10,000; the router sets it when omitted), `fromWalletId`, `toWalletId`, `recipient`, and `provisionMissingWallets` (create a receiving HivemindOS wallet on the destination chain if the account has none there; needs `wallets:create`).

Credits versus wallet assets
sections.text:
- Agent Credits pay for wallet creation, execution, signing, managed trading, and executed swaps from HivemindOS wallets. The server-owned pricing response sets the maximum charge.
- Wallet assets pay the transfer or trade amount and its network fee. The wallet policy sets which asset actions are allowed.
- `creditsPerDay` can add a key-level daily ceiling to wallet creation, transaction execution, signature execution, trading-order execution, and swap execution. See [limits](limits.html#daily-credit-limits).

HTTP 402 means the HivemindOS account balance is too low for the API charge. It says nothing about whether the wallet holds enough assets. Check both balances and show the right next step.
